title: Growing kohl rabi microgreens
subtitle: Mild, slightly sweet brassica cotyledons ready in 7 to 9 days
excerpt: Kohl rabi microgreens have a mild, slightly sweet flavour at the cotyledon stage, milder than radish or mustard and softer than kale. The cycle is 7 to 9 days on a 25 cm indoor tray.
sourceNotes: UMass Extension microgreens guides (open-access). Cornell Cooperative Extension indoor growing material. Standard microgreen-growing practice synthesised from extension service material.

glossaryTerms.definition: Watering by setting the growing tray inside a second tray filled with water, allowing the growing medium to draw moisture up from below. Keeps the seedling surface dry and reduces mould and damping-off risk in microgreen trays.

A fungal condition where seedling stems collapse and rot at the soil surface. Caused by Pythium, Fusarium, and Rhizoctonia species in warm, wet, poorly-ventilated conditions. Common in overcrowded or overwatered microgreen trays.

content.text: Kohl rabi microgreens are a year-round indoor tray crop with a cycle of 7 to 9 days. Sow on a 25 cm tray, blackout for two to three days, then bring to light and cut when the cotyledons are fully expanded. The flavour is mild and faintly sweet at this stage, distinctly softer than radish or mustard cotyledons.
Kohl rabi microgreens are a useful addition to a mixed microgreen tray where the assertive bite of radish or mustard needs tempering. They blend well with all brassica cotyledons.

Light: a bright south or west-facing windowsill in spring and summer. In winter, a supplementary LED grow light 15 to 20 cm above the tray at 14 hours per day gives the most uniform growth. Kohl rabi microgreens tolerate slightly lower light than broccoli but produce better stems under good light.
Temperature: 18 to 22°C. Room temperature is correct; cold drafts below 15°C slow germination noticeably.
Day 0: sow. Fill the tray with pre-dampened seed compost or coir to within 1 cm of the rim. Scatter kohl rabi seed at 15 to 20 g per 25 cm tray. Press gently into contact with the medium.
Days 1 to 3: blackout. Cover with a second tray, lightly weighted. Remove when shoots are 2 to 3 cm tall.
Day 4 onward: light. Cotyledons green up within 24 hours.
only from this point: set the tray inside a second tray with 1 to 2 cm of water and let the medium absorb it from below.
Days 7 to 9: cut. Cut 1 cm above the medium when cotyledons are fully open and 5 to 7 cm tall. Use fresh or refrigerate for up to two days.

attrs.heading: Troubleshooting
attrs.intro: Common problems on kohl rabi microgreen trays.

items.symptom: Stem rot at the base within the first few days
items.cause: Damping off from top-watering or poorly ventilated conditions.
items.fix: Bottom-water only, discard the tray, and restart.

items.cause: Seed too old, medium too dry, or cold room.
items.fix: Use fresh untreated seed. Warm the room to above 16°C. Keep the medium damp during the blackout phase.

items.symptom: Pale stems and slow greening after blackout
items.cause: Insufficient light or too long in the blackout.
items.fix: Move to better light or add a grow light. Remove the blackout cover as soon as the shoots are 2 to 3 cm tall.

content.text: Use untreated kohl rabi seed. Standard vegetable seed packets for kohl rabi often carry a fungicide coating; microgreen suppliers stock untreated seed in larger quantities.
is low risk if you bottom-water and keep the room ventilated.
